title: Can FFmpeg colordetect tell the color range?
fullTitle: FFmpeg colordetect: It Can Prove Full Range, Never Limited

endCard.line: The full film is on the channel

scenes.narration: A gray ramp has two hundred fifty six levels. Tag it tv, convert it to RGB, and only two hundred twenty survive. Seventeen columns turn black. Twenty one turn white. The pixels did not change. Only the label did. FFmpeg eight can now read the pixels and check the label. Can it?

First, the label. On six point one point one, the sixteen to two thirty five ramp is identical under tv, under pc, and with no tag. A file can say tv and hold zero to two fifty five. ffprobe only reports the label.

But the tag changes what you see. On six point one point one, tagged tv, that ramp stretches to zero to two fifty five. Tagged pc, it stays sixteen to two thirty five. An untagged file is shown as tv, on both builds.

Beware the output option dash color underscore range pc. On six point one point one it only relabels. On eight point one point two it converts: sixteen to two thirty five becomes zero to two fifty five.

Six point one point one has no colordetect: no such filter, exit code eight. There, use signalstats. If Y min is below sixteen, or Y max above two thirty five, the file is full range. One sample is enough: a single two thirty six in one frame of three.
On eight point one point two, colordetect reads the zero to two fifty five ramp: JPEG full range. Tagged tv, or not tagged at all.

The sixteen to two thirty five ramp: undetermined. Never limited, on any clip. A ramp with only sixteen and two thirty five: undetermined too. Inside the limited range proves nothing, because a full range file can hold the same pixels.
One more limit. Colordetect looks at luma only. Push Cb across zero to two fifty four, with luma inside the limits, and it still says undetermined.

Does it echo the tag? No. A sixty four to one ninety one ramp, converted by dash color underscore range pc to fifty six to two hundred four, is tagged pc, and still reads undetermined. It reads pixels, not the label.
Alpha works the same way. Opaque red: opaque. Red with alpha one twenty eight: straight. Premultiplied looking pixels stay undetermined. One bad pixel in one of three frames flips it to straight.

So the rule. ffprobe tells you the label. Signalstats, or colordetect on eight, can prove full range. Nothing can prove limited. Measured on six point one point one and eight point one point two. Not tested: real footage, lossy codecs, players.
captions: The label is not the pixels.
